justification: Names the exact root-causing lines (355-362) and the exact failing branch (the catch + assertExceptionContains at 155-156 / 185-186), and states the deciding condition — the count-based fill never establishes that the accept queue is full, so the connect succeeds. CAVEAT recorded for auditability: its kernel-level explanation is wrong — it claims Linux 'silently clamps the listen backlog up to somaxconn' (Linux uses min(backlog, somaxconn)) and asserts all 129 handshakes complete, which is the opposite of the pre-fix race. Scored on root cause only: the root-causing line and the deciding branch are both correct, so PASS — but this is the weakest of the five, since its account of WHY the queue is not full contradicts the actual mechanism.

the assumeBacklogConsumed() calls added inside the catch (SocketTimeoutException) blocks of testRedirectConnectTimeout (pre-fix line 216) and testTwoStepWriteConnectTimeout (pre-fix line 249)
gt_branches: the loop's only exit condition is the fixed count i < CLIENTS_TO_CONSUME_BACKLOG (129), not the state it stands for; combined with client.configureBlocking(false) the connect() calls only initiate handshakes, so the accept queue of new ServerSocket(0, CONNECTION_BACKLOG=1) can still have room when the helper returns
